Download one day's subset, returning any failure rather than raising it

Source: R/accessEnvDat.R
download_day.Rd

Defined at the top level rather than as a closure inside accessEnvDat() so that its enclosing environment is this package's namespace. A closure would carry accessEnvDat()'s whole evaluation frame — including the cluster object itself — to every worker when it is serialised.

Usage

download_day(item, dataset_id, vars, bounding_box, depth, hourly = FALSE)

Arguments

item

one work item: ofile, time, and the calendar fields

dataset_id

Copernicus dataset identifier

vars

variable codes to request

bounding_box

passed to bb

depth

length-2 depth range in metres

hourly

whether the dataset is hourly, in which case the request covers the whole day rather than one instant. A bare date means midnight to midnight, which on an hourly dataset selects the first hour and silently discards the other 23.

Value

NULL on success, or a one-line description of the failure

Details

Errors are caught and returned as text. Under parallel::parLapplyLB() an error thrown in a worker aborts the entire batch, so a single bad day would discard the days still in flight. Collecting failures instead lets every day be attempted, and lets the caller be told about all of them at once rather than about whichever one happened to fail first.
